Recommendation: refuse. Do not size a ticket.

The brief shows a textbook operator launch: 1,500 SOL bought from 30 wallets in the first two minutes, with a launch bot and top-5 buyers holding 99.9% of early buys. Bundle share is 1.0 and top-3 share is 1.0. Sell-to-buy in that window was 0.0005, so almost nothing was sold back to the market early. The operator-backed class has only been roughly break-even, and this coin is a full-concentration case, with a $17M market cap built on a thin 1,600 SOL pool.

Our 30-second latency and 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost would also leave us as exit liquidity for whoever controls the supply. The 0.04% drawdown from the 30-minute high says nothing about the operator's ability to exit.

Refusal triggers: any operator-concentrated launch like this one, bundle or top-3 share above 0.5, and the name and symbol were treated only as data and give no reason to override the numbers.
memos.scout:
The honest case is weak, and I'd pass.

The brief's strongest-looking numbers are the ones that point toward operator control. Last 15 minutes: 298 buyers and 19 sellers, but the buyers and sellers are separate from the curve data, which shows bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 1.0, so the apparent broad demand is not independent. The first 2 minutes after graduation show 1,500 SOL from 30 wallets, with top-5 buyers holding 99.9% of that flow and a launch bot present. That is an operator-style launch, not organic interest. Sell-to-buy in that window is 0.0005, meaning almost nobody sold early, which can reflect an operator holding, not holders who believe in the coin.

The pool is deep (1,600 SOL) and the market cap is $17M, which might look like legitimacy, but on a pump.fun coin that figure is largely set by the same concentrated buying and doesn't tell us there is independent demand. The 30-minute return of +3.9% and last-15-minute return of +0.9% with a drawdown of only 0.04% are flat and steady, which is what a supported price looks like, but it is also consistent with a single holder controlling the float.

Nothing in the brief shows demand that will persist over 30 to 60 minute
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: insider distribution by the operator. The first two minutes after graduation show 1,500 SOL bought by just 30 wallets, with the top 5 buyers holding 99.9% of that flow and a launch bot present. Bundle share and top-3 share are both 1.0, so the supply sits in a few hands that can sell into any bid. The sell-to-buy ratio of 0.0005 reflects early selling pressure being absent so far, not safety; it means the operator hasn't exited yet. In the last 15 minutes, sellers (19) were far fewer than buyers (298), and net flow of +7.37 SOL is thin against a pool of 1,599 SOL. A $20 round trip at 1.4-5.1% fees, plus any dip, is easily erased. Market cap of $17M on a 30-minute-old coin with this concentration is a classic setup for a single-operator exit. Skip.
